data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel produces more reliable judgments not through superior cognition, but via 'stochastic error cancellation' coordinated by the checklist, which can be distinguished from genuine reliability by the introduction of a 'plausible-but-wrong' decoy item.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel members are highly correlated in their errors (systemic bias), preventing the stochastic cancellation of mistakes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is so exhaustive that it leaves no room for 'judgment' other than binary verification.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist serves as a coordination mechanism that ensures all panel members look at the same features, while the 'panel' aspect allows random individual errors to cancel out (Law of Large Numbers).
